passage: L1.1: "Using the same dataset for training and testing the model is a textbook example of overfitting" (Results, 'Toward a solution: A taxonomy of data leakage', PMC10499856; as returned by the fetch tool, the rest of the sentence not verified verbatim).
faulty: Ridge regression (lambda 1.0 on standardised X, centred y, intercept) is fitted on all 100 rows; R-squared = 1 - SSE/SST of its fitted values on the same 100 rows; holds iff >= 0.10. No held-out rows.
fixed: 5-fold cross-validation, fold of row i = i mod 5; ridge (lambda 1.0, standardisation fitted on the training folds) fitted on 80 rows, predicts the 20 held-out rows; pooled R-squared = 1 - SSE/SST over all 100 held-out predictions (SST around the pooled mean of y); holds iff >= 0.10.
estimand: Faulty: the apparent (resubstitution) R-squared of a model fitted to all 100 samples. Fixed: the expected out-of-sample R-squared of the same model fitted on 80 samples and applied to new samples.
model_family: Ridge regression with fixed penalty 1.0 on standardised features, closed form (minimum-norm solution, defined when features > samples). Source names no model; chosen because it is numpy-only, deterministic and defined for 150 features on 100 samples.
sizes_note: Source states none. 100 x 150 = 15,000 values: small-n large-p regime, where the in-sample estimate is largest; the corrected check is 5 closed-form ridge fits per sample (seconds), far inside the 30-minute estimate. Dependence of the error's size on sample size or feature count: not stated.
exploited_structure: Many features relative to samples, so a fitted linear model reproduces the outcome of the very rows it was fitted on.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: 150 features / 100 samples is the brief's own size; set by the brief

notes: Guard: R-squared is undefined below 2 evaluated rows or when the variance of y is zero (return None); non-finite values return None. Statistic family differs from the earlier L1.1 combination (classification). Rule for fold assignment assumes rows are in arbitrary order.
